title: Group a bounded search and batch safe inspections
goal: Combine find pruning and grouped alternatives, then batch read-only inspection of the resulting regular files.
challenge: Within the supplied tree, inspect current .txt or .log regular files, pruning the old directory. Retain source checksums and show the mistaken precedence case. Never delete through find.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/textarchive-find.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && saved_umask=$(umask) && umask 077 && pwd && here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/textarchive-find.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700 && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w"; }; dir_ok() { test -d "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(realpath -e -- "$1")" = "$w/$1"; }; fresh() { for f; do test ! -e "$f" && test ! -L "$f" || return 19; done; }; here && test "$(df --output=avail -k . | tail -1)" -gt 65536
steps.explanation: Create and record a new private guest workspace. Stop on any failed guard; the free-space check is an observation, not a guaranteed reserve. Do not use the host terminal.
steps.expected: A unique learner-owned mode0700 directory; no originals overwritten.

steps.command:
here && fresh tree selected.txt wrong.txt original.sha && mkdir tree tree/old tree/dir.log && printf 'new
' > tree/'space name.txt' && printf 'event
' > tree/current.log && printf 'old
' > tree/old/stale.txt && sha256sum tree/'space name.txt' tree/current.log tree/old/stale.txt > original.sha
steps.explanation: All targets are a tiny declared tree. dir.log is deliberately a directory, so a suffix alone is insufficient.
steps.expected: Three original files and one misleading directory name.

steps.command: here && dir_ok tree && dir_ok tree/old && timeout -k 1s 8s find -P tree -path tree/old -prune -o -type f \( -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log' \) -exec sh -c 'for f; do printf "%s " "$f"; wc -c < "$f"; done' sh {} + > selected.txt && cat selected.txt
steps.explanation: -prune belongs before the alternative; grouped suffixes both require -type f. {} + batches pathname arguments without turning them into shell source. This inspection is read-only.
steps.expected: Only space name.txt(4 bytes) and current.log(6 bytes); old subtree and dir.log excluded.

steps.command: here && dir_ok tree && dir_ok tree/old && timeout -k 1s 8s find -P tree -type f -name '*.txt' -o -name '*.log' > wrong.txt && grep -qx tree/dir.log wrong.txt && sha256sum -c original.sha
steps.explanation: Without grouping, the .log alternative does not inherit -type f. This wrong query prints only; it does not mutate targets.
steps.expected: Wrong query includes dir.log, while every original checksum still matches.

hints: Use -P and restrict the root; do not add destructive actions.
review: I retained actual statuses, bytes and relevant identities, including the incorrect case; successful command exit alone is not my evidence.
